definition: NNUE, which stands for efficiently updatable neural network (often stylized as ƎUИИ) is a neural network made to replace the evaluation of Shogi, chess and other board games using alpha-beta searchers running on a CPU.
details: NNUE, which stands for efficiently updatable neural network (often stylized as ƎUИИ) is a neural network made to replace the evaluation of Shogi, chess and other board games using alpha-beta searchers running on a CPU.

explainer.lead: NNUE is a neural-network design for scoring board positions in games such as chess and Shogi. It lets an alpha-beta game engine use a neural evaluation on a CPU, with efficient updates as the search examines different positions.

tiers.eli5: Think of a chess engine with a fast lookup card it can update after each move instead of recomputing everything from scratch.
tiers.practitioner: It is used as the position evaluator inside a CPU alpha-beta searcher, with incremental updates as moves are made; the pitfall is that the update scheme constrains the network architecture.
tiers.paperLevel: A neural network designed to replace board-game evaluation for alpha-beta searchers running on a CPU. Limits: it targets CPU search rather than GPU-heavy evaluation.

components.name: Board position
components.detail: The game state that the engine needs to judge.

components.name: Efficiently updatable evaluation
components.detail: The neural network produces a position evaluation and is designed for efficient updates as the searched position changes.

components.name: Alpha-beta search
components.detail: The surrounding CPU-based search uses the evaluation when comparing lines of play.

flow: Alpha-beta search reaches or changes a board position.
NNUE evaluates the position, updating its evaluation efficiently.
The resulting score is returned to the search.
The search continues through further candidate positions.
explainer.lineage: NNUE replaces the evaluation function in CPU-based alpha-beta engines while leaving alpha-beta search in place.
explainer.whyItMatters: It brings neural position evaluation to board-game search without requiring the evaluation to be recomputed from scratch for every changing position.
